speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Next, the Mission Statement of the AGC reads as follows: "Serving Singapore's interests and upholding the rule of law through sound advice, effective representation, fair and independent prosecution and accessible legislation".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: There are two further observations I wish to make.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, we see senior AGC officers recruited from the private sector, such as from large law firms.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: A private sector lawyer may be briefed to go all out to protect his clients' interests, but an AGC officer should not simply go all out to ensure that the Government wins in Court but should serve Singapore's interests by promoting justice.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is common these days to see AGC officers refer to Government bodies in Court as their "client" and in correspondence as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Looking at the period from 2011, then-AG, Mr Sundaresh Menon, felt that AGC was understaffed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: His successor, Mr VK Rajah, took the same view as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: AGC raised it with the Ministry of Finance (MOF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This helped to "right-size" AGC and ensured that it could deliver quality legal services as required by the public sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The increase in manpower allocation was necessary, in view of the fact that AGC's portfolio and work demands have increased significantly over the past few years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, AGC has taken on an increased volume in complexity of civil and criminal hearings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In recent years, there has been a significant increase in complexity of white-collar crime cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There has also been an increase in sophisticated, organised and internationalised criminal activity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The complexity of legal advisory work has also grown, in tandem with the increasing multifaceted nature of the Government's work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The demand for legal input to improve and speed up the formulation and implementation of policies has also increased.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the international arena, AGC has managed an increasing number of disputes and negotiations to advance Singapore's interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: AGC has also taken on several new functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: AGC now provides legal representation for Statutory Boards in judicial review proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: AGC has taken over prosecution work from the Police's Prosecution Branch.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The AGC legislative team has embarked on the Plain Laws Understandable by Singaporeans (PLUS) project, an initiative to improve and modernise legislative drafting, to make our laws more accessible to the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked about mid-career recruits to the AGC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mid-career hires can bring along fresh perspectives and ideas honed by their experiences elsewhere.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The key considerations are whether the mid-career hires possess the necessary skills, aptitude and desire to serve the public interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We do not see any basis for suggesting that mid-career entrants will not serve the public interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It will be noted that many of our Judges are appointed to the Bench from the private sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Can it be suggested that they are all not suitable because they come from the private sector?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It will also be noted that some Cabinet Ministers are appointed from the private sector, including both officeholders in MinLaw.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Would Ms Lim suggest that they are not suitable because they were not in the public sector all their lives?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If she is saying − as a matter of institutional philosophy − that there is something inherent about the office of AG that rules out political affiliation at some time, then that will be inaccurate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In many first-world countries, the AG, as the head of AGC, is, in fact, a sitting Member of Parliament or politician.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the United Kingdom, the AG is a Cabinet Minister.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He is also the Chief Legal Adviser and also oversees the Prosecution Service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The AG is a member of the Legislature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the US, the President appoints an AG − and the current AG was a Republican Senator no less.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The US AG had taken positions on political issues as a Senator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He resigned from the Senate just before being appointed AG and continues to be a member of the Republican Party.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, as a matter of systems design, many countries see it perfectly proper to have an AG who is a politician.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, AGC must be led by the best legal talent available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our talent pool for the highest legal appointment is small.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is common for political parties to get the best legal talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some of our top lawyers have been Members of Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Look at the senior partners and top lawyers in our largest firms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Drew & Napier − Mr Davinder Singh Senior Counsel (SC), who is generally recognised as the top litigator in town, was a People's Action Party (PAP) Member of Parliament; Wong Partnership − the top litigator, Mr Alvin Yeo SC, was a PAP Member of Parliament; Allen & Gledhill − one of the two SCs in the litigation department, Mr Edwin Tong, is a sitting Member of Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If you look at Rajah & Tann − the current Chief Justice, as well as Judge of Appeal Steven Chong and Justice Quentin Loh came into public service, as well as the previous AG.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And, in the last few years, several others have also been taken from other firms and the private sector, to come into the Public Service.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In our view, those whom I mentioned, who are still in private practice, would all, together with Mr Hri Kumar SC, be considered to be among the top six to seven litigators in town.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This wealth of talent should be available to the Public Service.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ultimately, the most important considerations are the quality, character and integrity of the individuals appointed to lead AGC.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As stated earlier, Mr Hri Kumar is amongst the top six to seven litigators in Singapore today.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He is recommended in publications, such as Chambers Global and Asia-Pacific Legal 500.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He has been hailed as, I quote, "an extremely… impressive litigator".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Others have observed that, again I quote "few senior counsel … can rival the prowess of Hri Kumar …".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Senior figures in the profession have noted that he is "incisive, diligent, fair-minded", possesses "rare intellect" and is capable of "consummate advocacy".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Appointments to the Public Service must, of course, be based on ability.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He loses the privacy he enjoyed in private practice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He also now earns significantly less than what he used to earn.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We should be grateful that a person of such standing has agreed to dedicate himself to the public cause.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We should welcome his spirit of public service.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, the ultimate decider of cases is the Court, not AG.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: While AG takes a position on whether to prosecute, it is the Court that eventually decides on innocence or guilt.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is why, in many countries, it is perfectly acceptable for the AG to be a politician.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This will enable AGC to serve as a steadfast guardian of the public interest and a steward of the rule of law.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But I have three clarifications for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The first is, she mentioned that Mr Hri Kumar was the most eminently suitable candidate for the post of Deputy AG.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Is she by implication saying that the Government does not see any other candidate from the Legal Service that could fill that post?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second clarification is that the Senior Minister of State mentioned or was trying to say that AG or Deputy AG has a limited role because, ultimately, the decider would be the Courts.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, in that sense, the posts of AG and Deputy AG are something with vast power, in fact, vis-a-vis the Courts.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The third clarification is that I do not know whether the Minister is able to give an indication of whether should the Deputy AG be faced with a file that is politically charged or has political connotations, whether he would actually take the step of recusing himself, which I think it is quite a common procedure in other countries as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Is he the most eminently qualified for this position?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He is one of those six to seven.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I do not know whether the Member will be more comfortable with Mr Davinder Singh or Mr Alvin Yeo.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is a fact that the PAP gets the best lawyers on its side.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some of us come into Government, some of us go into − when I say "us", I mean litigators − the Bench, and some litigators do other kinds of public service.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah made the point that a couple in this top six, seven have previously indicated that they would prefer not to come into the Public Service.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The real issue is: is there something systemically wrong?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Ms Sylvia Lim waxed lyrical about the appointment process in the US, and Jeff Sessions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And they have a system where a sitting Republican Senator transfers over and becomes AG, absolutely no problems.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, I would say I do not see any issue with someone who has had a link in the past, for the very sound reasons that Ms Indranee Rajah has given.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Second, wide discretion, but in matters that go to Court, ultimately, the Court decides.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If exercise of discretion is required, of course, AGC decides − AG, Deputy AG, Solicitor-General – based on a variety of factors, and that is why you choose people of character and competence.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is a Government that builds up institutions, not pulls them down.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Third − should the Deputy AG disqualify himself?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There are clear rules on when lawyers should recuse themselves from particular matters and I am sure every lawyer in AGC is aware of the laws relating to recusal.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Sylvia Lim, do you wish to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: No, Madam, I wish to say that my reservations remain but, nevertheless, I do respect that AGC has to continue with its work, and I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
